newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japanese chemical firms merge to gain market edge.
newsitem.headline: Japanese chemical firms merge to gain market edge.

text.p: Prompted by increasingly fierce competition in the international chemical industry, two leading Japanese chemical companies announced on Monday that they would merge in October next year.

Mitsui Petrochemical Industries Ltd and Mitsui Toatsu Chemicals Inc said they would merge to become Mitsui Chemicals Inc, creating the second-largest chemical producer in Japan after Mitsubishi Chemical Corp.

"The two companies have decided to merge upon recognising that uniting our corporate resources is the best choice for surviving the global competition and expanding further," the companies said in a statement.
The companies announced last month that they were considering a merger.
They said Mitsui Toatsu would be dissolved and that 0.6 Mitsui Toatsu share would be exchanged for one Mitsui Petrochemical share.
The new company will have total assets of 1.03 trillion yen ($9.1 billion) and will be capitalised at 102.9 billion yen ($918 million), the statement said.
Mitsui Toatsu's president Akio Sato is expected to take the helm of the company, the statement said.
Analysts said the merger is aimed at boosting their ability to fend off increasingly fierce competition from European and U.S. chemical companies looking to expand into Asia.
The two merged companies' combined production capacity for phenol would be the world's second-largest, making up nine percent of the world market and half that in Japan, analysts said.
Phenol is used in making industrial parts and agricultural chemicals.
But analysts said the new company will be internationally competitive only if it can cut its workforce and production costs.
The merger will be the first major one in the Japanese chemical industry since October 1994, when two Mitsubishi group firms united to create Mitsubishi Chemical Corp. ($1=111 yen)
